items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: you’re going to play Bill Evans and Oscar Peterson, trios

ctx.x: But it’s ironic that I just got the last DownBeat issue and it’s the sort of where to go to school issue. And it’s hundreds, literally hundreds of schools, and they’re just the ones that decided to put an ad in the DownBeat. So if it doesn’t have much of a role, why is it that it’s been so elevated and embraced by academia?

Well I think academia needs money, they need people to come to school, and jazz has been, over the last sixty years, very popular with young musicians, this, that and the other, and the question has always been well if you graduate these people and they can play jazz what are they going to do? Because there’s never been enough opportunities for everybody to play. So I don’t know what they do. They seep over into doing other things and maybe they teach privately and maybe they play two nights a week instead of…

have about forty-two minutes. So I really need a listening class. That would help these people to appreciate it more, I know. But back to your question, academia and jazz — I don’t know. I just don’t know. I don’t know. You don’t hear it out. Here’s something I’d love to do. I’d love to get somebody with a whole lot of money and if we go to McDonald’s and Wendy’s and all these fast food places and say I will pay all of your BMI, your Muzak funds for five years. Three years. You don’t have to pay. You’re paying…

items.title: Aebersold Jamey — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember telling him... I said, “Ok, I’m going to play piano; what do you want to play?”... I stopped and I said, “Bill, you just need to learn your scales and your arpeggios...”

ctx.x: That’s before... Because I know Lyle Mays went to North Texas.

Yeah, right. That was probably after they came to the camp, I suspect. I can’t remember. But also, Bill Evans, the saxophone player that played Miles—he was from Chicago, and he came to the camp. I remember telling him... He wanted to get together a private lessons. So we put it off until the very last day, because I was busy. Then he came into the room, there were a bunch of people in there... I said, “Ok, I’m going to play piano; what do you want to play?” I think he said he wanted to play “I Can’t Get…
Around the world. I want to talk about that. Because Hans Gruber in Germany...
